description: Compare each channel's average fee rate to the overall average fee rate across all linked fee records.

b.request: For each order channel with linked fees, calculate that channel's average fee rate; identify channels whose average fee rate exceeds the global average fee rate across all linked fees; return a single row containing the mean of the above-average channels' average fee rates and the average amount by which these channels' mean rate exceeds the global average rate.
b.sql:
WITH global_avg AS (
  SELECT AVG(f.feerate) as global_avg_fee_rate
  FROM fees f
),
channel_avgs AS (
  SELECT o.exchspot, AVG(f.feerate) as channel_avg_fee_rate
  FROM orders o
  JOIN fees f ON o.recordvault = f.orderslink
  GROUP BY o.exchspot
),
above_avg_channels AS (
  SELECT ca.channel_avg_fee_rate, ga.global_avg_fee_rate
  FROM channel_avgs ca
  CROSS JOIN global_avg ga
  WHERE ca.channel_avg_fee_rate > ga.global_avg_fee_rate
)
SELECT 
  AVG(aac.channel_avg_fee_rate) as mean_of_above_average_rates,
  AVG(aac.channel_avg_fee_rate - aac.global_avg_fee_rate) as avg_excess_over_global
FROM above_avg_channels aac
b.raw: For each order channel with linked fees, calculate that channel's average fee rate; identify channels whose average fee rate exceeds the global average fee rate across all linked fees; return a single row containing the mean of the above-average channels' average fee rates and the average amount by which these channels' mean rate exceeds the global average rate.

c.request: For fees tied to orders (`fees.orderslink` = `orders.recordvault`), which order channels (`orders.orderbase`) have an above-average fee rate (`feerate`, ignoring missing values)? Give me one row: those channels' mean average fee rate and, on average, how far above average they are, unrounded. Compare each channel's average fee rate to the overall average fee rate across all linked fee records.
c.sql:
WITH channel_avgs AS (
  SELECT 
    o.orderbase,
    AVG(f.feerate) as channel_avg
  FROM fees f
  JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault
  WHERE f.feerate IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY o.orderbase
),
overall_avg_calc AS (
  SELECT AVG(f.feerate) as overall_avg
  FROM fees f
  WHERE f.orderslink IS NOT NULL AND f.feerate IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
  AVG(ca.channel_avg) as mean_fee_rate,
  AVG(ca.channel_avg - oa.overall_avg) as avg_distance_above_average
FROM channel_avgs ca
CROSS JOIN overall_avg_calc oa
WHERE ca.channel_avg > oa.overall_avg

d.request: Identify order channels whose mean fee rate exceeds the overall mean fee rate across all linked fee records, returning the mean fee rate of those above-average channels and their average margin above the overall mean.
d.sql:
WITH overall_mean AS (
  SELECT AVG(f.feerate) AS mean_fee_rate
  FROM fees f
  WHERE f.feerate IS NOT NULL
),
channel_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    o.orderbase,
    AVG(f.feerate) AS channel_mean_fee_rate
  FROM fees f
  JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault
  WHERE f.feerate IS NOT NULL AND o.orderbase IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY o.orderbase
)
SELECT
  cs.orderbase AS channel,
  cs.channel_mean_fee_rate,
  (cs.channel_mean_fee_rate - om.mean_fee_rate) AS avg_margin_above_overall_mean
FROM channel_stats cs
CROSS JOIN overall_mean om
WHERE cs.channel_mean_fee_rate > om.mean_fee_rate
ORDER BY cs.channel_mean_fee_rate DESC;

a.request: Looking at fees linked to orders (`fees.orderslink` = `orders.recordvault`), compute each order channel's (`orders.orderbase`) average fee rate (`feerate`, ignoring missing values), and use the average fee rate over all those linked fee records as the benchmark. For the channels whose average is strictly above that benchmark, return a single row with the mean of their average fee rates and the mean of how far each one exceeds the benchmark, unrounded.
a.sql:
WITH linked_fees AS (
  SELECT f.feerate, o.orderbase
  FROM fees f
  JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault
  WHERE f.feerate IS NOT NULL
),
channel_avgs AS (
  SELECT orderbase, AVG(feerate) as channel_avg
  FROM linked_fees
  GROUP BY orderbase
),
overall_avg AS (
  SELECT AVG(feerate) as benchmark
  FROM linked_fees
),
above_benchmark AS (
  SELECT c.channel_avg, (c.channel_avg - o.benchmark) as excess
  FROM channel_avgs c
  CROSS JOIN overall_avg o
  WHERE c.channel_avg > o.benchmark
)
SELECT AVG(channel_avg) as mean_avg_fee_rates, AVG(excess) as mean_excess
FROM above_benchmark
